answers.answer: To create a FunctionTool with typed parameters using Zod schemas, you use the ToolOptions interface which accepts both Zod v3 and v4 schemas. The FunctionTool constructor takes ToolOptions<TParameters> with fields: name (optional, auto-derived from function name if not provided), description (required), parameters (optional, can be z3.ZodObject, z4.ZodObject, Schema, or undefined), execute (the function to run), and isLongRunning (optional boolean). When parameters is a ZodObject, the tool automatically validates input using schema.parse() before calling the execute function. The zodObjectToSchema utility converts Zod schemas to Gemini Schema format, handling both v3 (using zod-to-json-schema) and v4 (using toJSONSchema from zod/v4), with post-processing to normalize to OpenAPI 3.0 format (uppercasing type names, converting numeric constraints to strings, removing unsupported fields).

AgentTool wraps an agent as a tool, allowing it to be called from within another agent. It takes AgentToolConfig with fields: agent (BaseAgent reference) and skipSummarization (optional boolean). Internally, AgentTool creates a new Runner instance with InMemorySessionService, InMemoryMemoryService, and a ForwardingArtifactService that forwards artifact operations to the parent's ToolContext. When executed, it creates a temporary session with the parent's session state (toolContext.state.toRecord()), runs the sub-agent with the user's message (JSON.stringify(args) if inputSchema is set, otherwise args['request']), and forwards stateDelta updates back to the parent via toolContext.state.update(). The skipSummarization option, when true, sets toolContext.actions.skipSummarization = true to prevent the model from summarizing the agent's output. The tool's declaration uses the agent's inputSchema if available (for LlmAgent), otherwise defaults to a simple {request: string} parameter. For non-Gemini-API variants, it also sets a response schema.

MCPToolset and MCPTool provide integration with Model Context Protocol servers. MCPToolset extends BaseToolset and takes MCPConnectionParams (union of StdioConnectionParams or StreamableHTTPConnectionParams) and optional ToolPredicate/string[] filter. StdioConnectionParams has type: 'StdioConnectionParams', serverParams (StdioServerParameters), and optional timeout. StreamableHTTPConnectionParams has type: 'StreamableHTTPConnectionParams', url (string), optional deprecated header field (replaced by transportOptions.requestInit.headers), timeout, sseReadTimeout, terminateOnClose, and transportOptions (StreamableHTTPClientTransportOptions). MCPSessionManager manages MCP client sessions using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, creating Client instances and connecting via StdioClientTransport or StreamableHTTPClientTransport based on connection type. MCPToolset.getTools() calls session.listTools() and wraps each MCP tool in an MCPTool instance. MCPTool translates MCP tool schemas to Gemini format using toGeminiSchema() which recursively converts MCP JSON schemas (handling nullable types via anyOf, inferring missing types, mapping types like 'text'/'string' to Type.STRING). When executed, MCPTool creates a session, sends a callTool request with the tool name and arguments, and returns the CallToolResult.

GoogleSearchTool is a built-in tool for Gemini models that retrieves search results from Google Search. Unlike FunctionTool which adds a FunctionDeclaration to the LLM request, GoogleSearchTool's processLlmRequest() adds a Tool config object directly to llmRequest.config.tools. For Gemini 1.x models, it adds {googleSearchRetrieval: {}} and throws an error if other tools are present (as Gemini 1.x doesn't support mixing search with other tools). For Gemini 2+ models, it adds {googleSearch: {}}. The tool validates the model is a Gemini model using isGemini1Model() and isGeminiModel() checks. Since this is a server-side built-in tool triggered by request parameters, the runAsync() method simply returns Promise.resolve() without performing any local execution. A global GOOGLE_SEARCH instance is exported for convenience.

ToolContext extends CallbackContext and provides tools with access to the invocation context, session state, and various operations. Key capabilities include: 1) Session state access via inherited state property and get/set methods. 2) Artifact operations: loadArtifact(filename, version?) to load artifacts, saveArtifact(filename, artifact) to save artifacts (returns version number), listArtifacts() to list artifact filenames. 3) Memory search via searchMemory(query) which calls invocationContext.memoryService.searchMemory() and returns SearchMemoryResponse with matching memories. 4) Credential requests via requestCredential(authConfig) which stores the auth request in eventActions.requestedAuthConfigs[functionCallId] for later resolution, and getAuthResponse(authConfig) to retrieve resolved credentials from session state using AuthHandler. 5) Tool confirmation via requestConfirmation({hint?, payload?}) which creates a ToolConfirmation object and stores it in eventActions.requestedToolConfirmations[functionCallId]. The ToolContext also exposes the functionCallId (used to map responses to calls) and actions property (alias for eventActions).

beforeToolCallback and afterToolCallback are callback hooks for LlmAgent that intercept tool execution. They are defined as SingleBeforeToolCallback and SingleAfterToolCallback types. The execution flow in handleFunctionCallList() has early-exit semantics: 1) Plugin beforeToolCallback runs first via pluginManager.runBeforeToolCallback(). If it returns a non-null value, that becomes the function response and subsequent callbacks are skipped. 2) If plugins don't override, canonical beforeToolCallbacks array is iterated. If any callback returns a non-null value, iteration stops and that value is used. 3) If no override is provided, the actual tool.runAsync() is called. 4) After execution (or override), plugin afterToolCallback runs via pluginManager.runAfterToolCallback(). If it returns a non-null value, that replaces the function response. 5) If plugins don't override, canonical afterToolCallbacks array is iterated until one returns a non-null value. The key pattern is that any non-null/non-undefined return short-circuits the rest of the callback chain. Plugins always run before canonical callbacks, and returning a value prevents canonical callbacks from executing.

BaseToolset is an abstract class that enables dynamic tool discovery and filtering. It has a constructor that accepts toolFilter (ToolPredicate function or string array). ToolPredicate is a function type: (tool: BaseTool, readonlyContext: ReadonlyContext) => boolean that decides whether a tool should be exposed to the LLM. The abstract getTools(context?: ReadonlyContext) method must be implemented by subclasses to return Promise<BaseTool[]>. The protected isToolSelected(tool, context) method applies the filter: if toolFilter is a function, it calls the predicate; if it's a string array, it checks if tool.name is in the array; if no filter is set, it returns true. BaseToolset differs from BaseTool in that BaseTool represents a single concrete tool with runAsync() execution logic, while BaseToolset represents a collection of tools with dynamic discovery (getTools() can query external sources like MCP servers). BaseToolset also has processLlmRequest(toolContext, llmRequest) for toolset-level LLM request processing and abstract close() method for cleanup. Subclasses like MCPToolset implement getTools() to discover tools from external sources.

Long-running tools are tools that may take significant time to complete and return results asynchronously. The mechanism includes: 1) BaseTool has an isLongRunning boolean property (default false) set via BaseToolParams. 2) LongRunningFunctionTool extends FunctionTool and automatically sets isLongRunning: true in its constructor, and appends a note to the tool description warning the model not to call the tool again if it has already returned intermediate/pending status. 3) During function call handling in handleFunctionCallList(), if tool.isLongRunning is true and functionResponse is null/undefined, the loop continues without creating a function response event (allowing the tool to return null and have the agent continue). 4) Function call IDs for long-running tools are tracked in longRunningToolIds Set using getLongRunningFunctionCalls() which checks if tools in toolsDict have isLongRunning=true. 5) Events can have a longRunningToolIds array field that lists the IDs of long-running tool calls. 6) This interacts with session resumption where the agent can be resumed later when the long-running tool completes, with the tool providing the result via a separate mechanism.

Tool confirmation allows tools to request user confirmation before execution. The mechanism involves: 1) ToolContext.requestConfirmation({hint?, payload?}) creates a ToolConfirmation object with hint (string explanation), confirmed (boolean, initially false), and payload (custom JSON-serializable data). 2) The ToolConfirmation is stored in eventActions.requestedToolConfirmations[functionCallId]. 3) After tools execute, generateRequestConfirmationEvent() checks functionResponseEvent.actions.requestedToolConfirmations. For each confirmation request, it creates a special function call with name REQUEST_CONFIRMATION_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME ('adk_request_confirmation'), args containing originalFunctionCall and toolConfirmation, and a generated client-side function call ID. These are marked as long-running tools. 4) The RequestConfirmationLlmRequestProcessor (referenced in llm_agent.ts and functions.ts) handles the confirmation round-trip: it intercepts these special function calls, likely prompts the user/client for confirmation, and when confirmed, resumes the original tool execution. 5) The confirmation event is yielded back to the client with the longRunningToolIds array populated, allowing the client to handle the confirmation UI and respond appropriately.
code_snippets: export const REQUEST_CONFIRMATION_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME = 'adk_request_confirmation';

answers.answer: The pauseOnToolCalls option in RunConfig enables client-side tool execution by allowing the agent loop to suspend on any tool call. When set to true (default is false), the agent execution pauses whenever tools are about to be called, yielding control back to the client. The client can then inspect the tool calls, decide whether to execute them, potentially modify arguments, execute tools client-side, and provide the results back to resume the agent. This is part of the Client-Side Tool Execution pattern. The RunConfig interface defines pauseOnToolCalls as an optional boolean with the description: 'If true, the agent loop will suspend on ANY tool call, allowing the client to intercept and execute tools (Client-Side Tool Execution).' The default value is set to false in createRunConfig(). This feature is distinct from long-running tools and provides a general mechanism for the client to control all tool execution rather than having the agent execute tools automatically.

BaseLlm is an abstract class that defines the LLM contract in ADK-JS. It has a constructor that takes {model: string} parameter. The core method is generateContentAsync(llmRequest: LlmRequest, stream?: boolean): AsyncGenerator<LlmResponse, void> which yields LlmResponse objects. When stream=true, it yields multiple partial responses; when false, it yields a single complete response. The connect(llmRequest: LlmRequest): Promise<BaseLlmConnection> method creates a live/bidirectional connection to the LLM for real-time interaction. The maybeAppendUserContent(llmRequest: LlmRequest) method ensures the LLM can continue generating output by appending a user message if: 1) contents array is empty, it adds 'Handle the requests as specified in the System Instruction.', or 2) the last content role is not 'user', it adds 'Continue processing previous requests as instructed. Exit or provide a summary if no more outputs are needed.' This prevents the model from stalling when it needs a user turn to continue. BaseLlm also has a static supportedModels property (array of string/RegExp patterns for LLMRegistry), a protected trackingHeaders property that returns client tracking headers ('x-goog-api-client', 'user-agent'), and a BASE_MODEL_SYMBOL for type checking via isBaseLlm().

The Gemini class implements BaseLlm for Google's Gemini models. Constructor takes GeminiParams: model (defaults to 'gemini-2.5-flash'), apiKey, vertexai (boolean), project, location, headers. Initialization logic (geminiInitParams function) checks: if vertexai is not set, it reads GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI env var; for Vertex AI mode, it requires project (from GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT) and location (from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION); for API key mode, it reads GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY env vars. The apiClient getter lazily creates GoogleGenAI instances: for Vertex AI mode with vertexai, project, location, httpOptions; for API key mode with apiKey and httpOptions. The apiBackend getter returns GoogleLLMVariant.VERTEX_AI or GoogleLLMVariant.GEMINI_API based on apiClient.vertexai. generateContentAsync() implements both streaming and non-streaming: preprocessing via preprocessRequest() (removes labels and displayName for Gemini API mode), calls maybeAppendUserContent(), then either generateContentStream() or generateContent(). For streaming, it accumulates thought text (parts with thought:true) and regular text separately, yielding partial responses with partial:true flag, and flushing accumulated text when switching between thought and regular content or on STOP finish reason. Non-streaming yields a single createLlmResponse(). The connect() method configures liveConnectConfig with systemInstruction and tools, then calls liveApiClient.live.connect() to create a GeminiLlmConnection for bidirectional streaming.

LLMRegistry is a factory/registry pattern that maps model names to BaseLlm implementations. It has a static llmRegistryDict: Map<string | RegExp, BaseLlmType> that stores regex patterns mapped to LLM classes. The static register<T extends BaseLlm>(llmCls) method iterates through llmCls.supportedModels array and registers each pattern via _register(). The resolve(model: string) method searches llmRegistryDict entries, creating a RegExp anchored with ^ and $ to replicate Python's re.fullmatch, testing if the pattern matches the model string. It uses an LRUCache (max size 32) to cache resolved model->class mappings for performance. The cache uses Map insertion order for LRU eviction. The newLlm(model: string) method calls resolve(model) and instantiates the resolved class with {model}. Gemini and ApigeeLlm are auto-registered at module load time (bottom of registry.ts). Gemini.supportedModels includes patterns: /gemini-.*/, /projects\/.+\/locations\/.+\/endpoints\/.+/ (fine-tuned endpoints), and /projects\/.+\/locations\/.+\/publishers\/google\/models\/gemini.+/ (Vertex Gemini long names). ApigeeLlm.supportedModels is [/apigee\/.*/]. Custom LLMs extend BaseLlm, define static supportedModels, and call LLMRegistry.register(CustomLlm).

ApigeeLlm extends Gemini to integrate with Apigee API gateway as a proxy for Gemini/Vertex AI models. It supports model name patterns matching /apigee\/.*/ with the format: apigee/[<provider>/][<version>/]<model_id> where provider is optional ('vertex_ai' or 'gemini'), version is optional API version (e.g., 'v1', 'v1beta'), and model_id is required (e.g., 'gemini-2.5-flash'). Examples: 'apigee/gemini-2.5-flash', 'apigee/v1/gemini-2.5-flash', 'apigee/vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash', 'apigee/gemini/v1/gemini-2.5-flash', 'apigee/vertex_ai/v1beta/gemini-2.5-flash'. Constructor takes ApigeeLlmParams (extends GeminiParams) with additional proxyUrl field (or APIGEE_PROXY_URL env var). The apigeeToGeminiInitParams() function determines vertexai mode by checking if model starts with 'apigee/vertex_ai/', and if not Vertex AI and no API key is provided, it uses fake key '-' (as Apigee handles auth). It overrides getHttpOptions() and getLiveHttpOptions() to set opts.baseUrl = this.proxyUrl, routing requests through Apigee. The identifyApiVersion() method parses the model string to extract the version, defaulting to 'v1beta1' for Vertex AI or 'v1alpha' for Gemini. Before calling super.generateContentAsync() or super.connect(), it extracts the model ID using getModelId() which removes the 'apigee/' prefix and provider/version components.

LlmRequest is an interface representing the request sent to an LLM. It has fields: model (optional string, the model name), contents (Content[] array of conversation messages), config (optional GenerateContentConfig with additional request settings), liveConnectConfig (LiveConnectConfig for live connections), and toolsDict ({[key: string]: BaseTool} dictionary mapping tool names to tool instances, excluded from JSON serialization). Note: tools in config should not be set directly; use utility functions instead. The appendInstructions(llmRequest, instructions: string[]) function joins the instructions array with '\n\n' and appends to config.systemInstruction, or sets it if not present. The appendTools(llmRequest, tools: BaseTool[]) function iterates through tools, calls tool._getDeclaration() to get FunctionDeclaration objects, adds them to toolsDict, and pushes a {functionDeclarations: [...]} object to config.tools array. The setOutputSchema(llmRequest, schema: SchemaUnion) function sets config.responseSchema = schema and config.responseMimeType = 'application/json' to enable JSON mode output.

LlmResponse is an interface representing the response from an LLM. It contains: content (optional Content, the response content from the first candidate), groundingMetadata (optional GroundingMetadata, grounding information), partial (optional boolean, indicates text is part of an unfinished stream, only for streaming mode with plain text), turnComplete (optional boolean, indicates response completeness, streaming mode only), errorCode (optional string, error code if response is an error, varies by model), errorMessage (optional string, error message text), interrupted (optional boolean, flag indicating LLM was interrupted during generation, usually due to user interruption in bidi streaming), customMetadata (optional {[key: string]: unknown}, custom key-value labels, must be JSON serializable), usageMetadata (optional GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata, token usage info), finishReason (optional FinishReason, reason for completion), liveSessionResumptionUpdate (optional LiveServerSessionResumptionUpdate, session resumption info), inputTranscription (optional Transcription, audio transcription of user input), outputTranscription (optional Transcription, audio transcription of model output). The createLlmResponse(response: GenerateContentResponse) function converts GenerateContentResponse to LlmResponse: if candidates exist and have content with parts, it returns {content, groundingMetadata, usageMetadata, finishReason}; if candidate exists but no content, it returns {errorCode: finishReason, errorMessage: finishMessage}; if promptFeedback exists, it returns {errorCode: blockReason, errorMessage: blockReasonMessage}; otherwise it returns {errorCode: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR'}.

To register a custom LLM implementation, you: 1) Create a class that extends BaseLlm. 2) Define a static readonly supportedModels property containing an array of string literals or RegExp patterns that match model names this LLM supports. 3) Implement the constructor with signature: constructor({model}: {model: string}), typically calling super({model}). 4) Implement abstract generateContentAsync(llmRequest: LlmRequest, stream?: boolean): AsyncGenerator<LlmResponse, void> to handle content generation. 5) Implement abstract connect(llmRequest: LlmRequest): Promise<BaseLlmConnection> for live connections. 6) Call LLMRegistry.register(YourCustomLlm) to register the class. The register method accepts a type that satisfies: (new (params: {model: string}) => T) & {readonly supportedModels: Array<string | RegExp>}, where T extends BaseLlm. Example pattern: class MyLlm extends BaseLlm { static override readonly supportedModels = [/my-model-.*/]; constructor({model}: {model: string}) { super({model}); } async *generateContentAsync(llmRequest, stream) { /* implementation */ } async connect(llmRequest) { /* implementation */ } } LLMRegistry.register(MyLlm);

GoogleLLMVariant is an enum with two values: GEMINI_API (for using API Key from Google AI Studio) and VERTEX_AI (for using credentials from Google Vertex AI). The variant is determined by getGoogleLlmVariant() which checks the GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI environment variable. The variant affects request preprocessing in Gemini.preprocessRequest(): for GEMINI_API variant (apiBackend === GoogleLLMVariant.GEMINI_API), it removes the labels property from llmRequest.config by setting labels = undefined (as Google AI Studio doesn't support labels), and removes displayName from all Blob/FileData objects in content parts by setting displayName = undefined (as displayName is Vertex AI specific). For VERTEX_AI variant, these fields are preserved. This preprocessing ensures requests are compatible with each backend's requirements. The apiBackend property is determined from apiClient.vertexai: if true, it's VERTEX_AI; otherwise GEMINI_API.

The Session interface has structure: id (string, unique identifier), appName (string, application name), userId (string, user ID), state (Record<string, unknown>, session state dictionary), events (Event[], array of events like user input, model response, function calls/responses), lastUpdateTime (number, last update timestamp). Sessions are created via BaseSessionService.createSession(request: CreateSessionRequest) which takes CreateSessionRequest with fields: appName (required string), userId (required string), state (optional Record<string, unknown> for initial state), sessionId (optional string, auto-generated if not provided). The method returns Promise<Session>. The createSession utility function (in session.ts) creates a Session object from Partial<Session> & {id, appName}, filling in defaults: userId defaults to '', state defaults to {}, events defaults to [], lastUpdateTime defaults to 0. Example implementation in InMemorySessionService generates a session ID via randomUUID() if not provided, stores the session in a nested map structure (appName -> userId -> sessionId -> Session), and merges app-level and user-level state before returning via mergeState().

The State class maintains current value and pending delta, with three prefixes for state keys: State.APP_PREFIX = 'app:' (application-wide state), State.USER_PREFIX = 'user:' (user-scoped state), State.TEMP_PREFIX = 'temp:' (temporary state excluded from persistence). Constructor takes value (current state Record) and delta (pending changes Record). Key methods: get<T>(key, defaultValue?) checks delta first, then value, returning defaultValue if not found; set(key, value) updates both value and delta; has(key) checks if key exists in value or delta; hasDelta() returns true if delta has keys; update(delta) merges delta into both this.delta and this.value using spread operator; toRecord() returns merged {...value, ...delta}. The temp: prefix exclusion happens in BaseSessionService.updateSessionState() which iterates event.actions.stateDelta and skips keys starting with State.TEMP_PREFIX (key.startsWith(State.TEMP_PREFIX)), preventing them from being saved to session.state. This allows transient data to be passed in stateDelta without persisting to the session. InMemorySessionService further separates app: and user: prefixed keys into separate storage (appState and userState dictionaries), merging them back when sessions are retrieved.

BaseSessionService defines abstract methods: createSession(request: CreateSessionRequest): Promise<Session> creates a new session; getSession(request: GetSessionRequest): Promise<Session | undefined> retrieves a session by appName/userId/sessionId with optional GetSessionConfig (numRecentEvents, afterTimestamp); getOrCreateSession(request: CreateSessionRequest): Promise<Session> (non-abstract) tries getSession first, creates if not found; listSessions(request: ListSessionsRequest): Promise<ListSessionsResponse> lists sessions for an appName/userId pair; deleteSession(request: DeleteSessionRequest): Promise<void> removes a session; appendEvent({session, event}: AppendEventRequest): Promise<Event> appends events to sessions. The base appendEvent implementation: 1) Returns immediately if event.partial is true (partial events aren't persisted). 2) Calls updateSessionState() which iterates event.actions.stateDelta, skipping temp: prefixed keys, and updates session.state with remaining keys. 3) Pushes the event to session.events array. 4) Returns the event. Subclasses like InMemorySessionService override appendEvent to add lastUpdateTime updates and separate app:/user: prefixed state into dedicated storage dictionaries (appState and userState), calling super.appendEvent() on the storage session object.

InMemorySessionService implements in-memory session storage using nested Record objects: sessions (appName -> userId -> sessionId -> Session), userState (appName -> userId -> key -> value for user: prefixed state), appState (appName -> key -> value for app: prefixed state). It stores sessions completely in memory without persistence. GetSessionConfig options control event filtering when retrieving sessions: numRecentEvents (number) limits events to the last N events via copiedSession.events.slice(-config.numRecentEvents); afterTimestamp (number) filters events to only those after the specified timestamp by iterating backwards through events, finding the last event before the timestamp, and slicing from that point forward (copiedSession.events.slice(i + 1)). The getSession implementation returns a cloneDeep() copy of the session with filtering applied, then calls mergeState() to merge app: and user: prefixed state from separate storage back into the session state. listSessions returns session metadata without events or state (creates Session objects with empty events and state). createSession generates a UUID if sessionId not provided, stores the session, and merges app/user state before returning.

The session service registry is implemented in core/src/sessions/registry.ts with the getSessionServiceFromUri(uri: string): BaseSessionService function. It supports URI schemes to select session service implementations. Currently, the only supported scheme is 'memory://' for in-memory sessions, checked via isInMemoryConnectionString(uri) which tests uri === 'memory://'. If matched, it returns new InMemorySessionService(). For any other URI, it throws Error('Unsupported session service URI: ${uri}'). This registry pattern allows for easy extension to support additional storage backends (like cloud storage, databases) by registering new URI schemes and corresponding service implementations. The pattern mirrors the artifact service registry (getArtifactServiceFromUri) which supports 'gs://bucket-name' for GCS and 'memory://' schemes.

The Runner passes stateDelta from the user's request to the session via createEventActions in the runAsync lifecycle. In Runner.runAsync(), after setting up the session and invocation context, if the user provides stateDelta in params, it creates a user event with createEvent() that includes actions: stateDelta ? createEventActions({stateDelta}) : undefined. This user event is then appended to the session via sessionService.appendEvent({session, event}). The createEventActions({stateDelta}) function creates an EventActions object with the provided stateDelta dictionary, along with empty artifactDelta, requestedAuthConfigs, and requestedToolConfirmations. When the event is appended, BaseSessionService.appendEvent() calls updateSessionState() which iterates the stateDelta entries, skipping temp: prefixed keys, and updates session.state[key] = value for each remaining key. State accumulation across multiple events works through this iterative process: each event's stateDelta is merged into session.state, so subsequent events see the accumulated state. The State class in InvocationContext maintains both value (current accumulated state) and delta (pending changes for this turn), with update() merging new deltas into both. This allows state to build up across the conversation while tracking what changed in each turn.
